rationale: The product of rank(net external financing) and rank(intangible intensity) is essentially the well-documented net-financing anomaly crossed with the equally well-documented R&D-intensity anomaly, and the expected positive sign directly contradicts the established negative pricing of net external financing, so the composite's predicted direction is at odds with its dominant component.

This is a defensible conditional refinement of the net-stock-issuance anomaly whose sign and construction are internally consistent, but the incremental content over plain net issuance is modest and the indicator forces all non-accelerating firms to exactly zero, so the spread may be driven mostly by the familiar issuance leg rather than the R&D-acceleration condition.

The hypothesis and expression are consistent and the creditor-screening mechanism for persistent R&D programs is a genuine interaction rather than a rediscovery, but the triple product of non-negative terms is heavily zero-inflated (all non-R&D or non-issuing firms collapse to a single point mass) and the expected positive sign runs against the documented negative debt-issuance effect, so a within-R&D-firm normalization would be a fairer test.

Debt-financed goodwill growth is close to a repackaging of the asset-growth and acquisition-underperformance literature, but the explicit financing-source conditioning is a legitimate incremental interaction with a coherent negative sign and a clean non-negative construction.

This substantially overlaps Joint Funding Deployment in ingredients, imposes a triple non-negative product that concentrates most firms at exactly zero, and predicts a positive sign for gross equity issuance in high-R&D, growing-sales firms — precisely the population the issuance and growth-glamour anomalies say underperforms — so the expected direction is poorly justified.

This is the most genuinely novel construction here, with a coherent financing-mismatch mechanism and a signed core term scaled by intangible intensity, but note the internal tension that the short leg (equity-dominant, high-intangible firms) is exactly the set the net-issuance anomaly predicts should underperform, so the negative expected sign may be fighting a strong known effect and should be diagnosed leg-by-leg.
